crime: Every evening a girl walked the perimeter wall, scraping its mortar with a sharpened spoon, and {WITCH_NAME} was the only one she let walk beside her. For each evening the wall held, she chalked a tick on the stone by her bunk.
At 7:40 one evening she showed {WITCH_NAME} a loose stone. "One of these evenings I'll go over without you," she said. "I won't say which, so you'll never have to lie for me."

{WITCH_NAME}'s mother had waved to her at the school gate one ordinary Wednesday: "See you at six." At noon a truck crossed the center line, and she never came home. The last day had looked like every other day.

At 7:55, in the girl's cell, she was chalking the evening's tick when {WITCH_NAME} laid a palm on the back of her neck. "Then it's tonight," {WITCH_NAME} said, "and I'll know which night." Her Magic put the girl straight into a deep sleep. {WITCH_NAME} drove the girl's own spoon under her ribs and tucked the blanket over her where she lay facing the wall. From 8:10 she sat among the girls in the lounge until lockup.

At 9:30 the girl's roommate came in, found her asleep facing the wall after the night's tick, breathing evenly, and said goodnight. At six in the morning the roommate woke to find her cold, with a small wound under her ribs and blood soaked into the mattress.
In the trial court, the prisoners went by the roommate's account: a girl sleeping that peacefully at 9:30 could not have been stabbed yet. They ruled she was stabbed after lockup.

Then a prisoner noticed the last chalk tick. It ran in one long line down the stone to the pillow. Nobody drifts off in the middle of a stroke. The prisoners understood: {WITCH_NAME}'s palm had taken the girl mid-tick, before {WITCH_NAME} ever left the cell, and the girl had slept straight through the spoon.
fields.epitaph: She had to know which evening it would be, and understood too late that not knowing was the gift.
execution: The execution stand raised a ring of perimeter-wall stones around her and mortared her arms flat at her sides into the first course. Course by course, the stones rose up her body, each one pressed tight with mortar, closing over her chest, then her shoulders. She strained her palm toward her own brow, but the stones held her arm. She stayed awake as the last course closed over her face. The sealed column stood silent, like any ordinary stretch of wall.

magic.name: Lullaby Palm
magic.text: Anyone her palm rests on, herself included, falls at once into deep, peaceful sleep.
